findings_addressed: plan-0.8.20.md §3a leg 1/3 — requirements + acceptance criteria + design + RED tests, NO implementation code. Delivered as dev/design/0.8.20-slice-31-sbom-survey-tool.md (spec of record: §3 requirements REQ-1..REQ-14, §4 the 22 AC->test map, §5 the design) plus scripts/sbom-survey/{README.md,tests/}.

§5.1 discovery — git ls-files-derived, never a filesystem walk. The 28 tracked manifests at cbb56212 are enumerated in the design with the reproduction command. python/pyproject.toml is UNTRACKED (.gitignore:88 /python/, root-anchored; the directory does not exist in the worktree) and is therefore OUT of BOM scope — the exact 'noise against gitignored dev/eval lockfiles' trap LIBRARY-BUMP-STEWARD.md §2 warns about. AC-SBOM-01/02/03.

§5.2 fixture manifests — the 4 dev/release/fixtures/cargo-skew/**/Cargo.toml and 4 dev/release/fixtures/pip-skew/**/setup.py are EXCLUDED from the BOM by an action="exclude" rule in the tracked tiers.toml, and every exclusion is RECORDED in survey.excluded (auditable, not invisible). Not a fourth tier: that would re-litigate the HITL tier ruling and put phantom packages in front of a vulnerability feed. Data-driven-ness is PROVEN by AC-SBOM-06, which loads a tier map with the rule removed and asserts the outcome changes — a hardcoded path check cannot satisfy it. Free consequence: no setup.py execution/AST parsing is ever needed.

§5.3 tiering — longest-prefix-wins over a tracked scripts/sbom-survey/tiers.toml (shape frozen in the design), with NO catch-all rule. An untiered tracked manifest raises UntieredManifestError NAMING THE PATH (AC-SBOM-07) and the CLI exits 2 naming it on stderr (AC-SBOM-21); AC-SBOM-08 asserts the repo's own map covers everything discovered, so a manifest added tomorrow goes red until somebody tiers it. Vocabulary stays exactly the three ruled values (AC-SBOM-09); eval-only currently matches nothing and is kept so a newly-tracked eval manifest cannot be silently absorbed into shipped.

§5.4 published-version seam — PublishedVersionSource protocol with Offline/Static/HttpRegistry implementations; run_survey takes `published` as a REQUIRED keyword-only argument with NO default, so no code path reaches the network implicitly (AC-SBOM-14 proves zero socket I/O by making socket.socket raise). status='current' is reachable ONLY from a successfully parsed pair on both sides; None/raise/unparseable all map to 'unknown'. The worst failure gets two named tests: AC-SBOM-15 (offline -> every row unknown, none current) and AC-SBOM-16 (raising source -> unknown + lookup_error recorded, no crash, no fallback to current).

§5.5 library<->library edges — direct lockfile parse (Cargo.lock, package-lock.json v3 packages map, uv.lock via stdlib tomllib/json); NO cargo metadata / npm ls subprocess, for hermeticity, fidelity to what is committed, and cost. Direct-vs-transitive is recovered from the tracked manifests' dependency tables (LBS §2's triage question). Honest limitation recorded: cargo lock edges are feature-resolved and lose normal/dev/build, so lock-derived edges are tagged edge-kind=resolved. AC-SBOM-12/13.

§5.6 durable home — generated reports go to the gitignored scripts/sbom-survey/out/; Slice 33's FINDINGS get the tracked home dev/design/0.8.20-slice-33-library-sweep-3-findings.md (design-doc convention, per the dev/design/0.8.20-sqlite-vec-99-vec0-delete-probe.md precedent) plus dev/plans/runs/0.8.20-slice-33-output.json and a DOC-INDEX row. The findings doc's six-section shape is fixed in the design so Slice 33 does not have to design it. AC-SBOM-18 asserts the report dir IS gitignored and the findings path is NOT.

§5.7 named external libraries with exact distribution names + constraints: cyclonedx-python-lib[json-validation] >=8.0,<9.0 · packageurl-python >=0.15,<1.0 · packaging >=24.0,<26.0 · semver >=3.0,<4.0 · pytest >=8.0,<10.0 (dev-only). Deliberately NOT taken, each justified: no HTTP client (stdlib urllib for three GET-JSON endpoints), no TOML library (stdlib tomllib, hence python>=3.11), no jsonschema (the json-validation extra already binds the right schema), no GitPython, no setup.py/AST tooling.

§5.8 forward compatibility with Slice 33 — staleness.json rows carry ecosystem, name, tier, depth, locked_version, latest_version, status, lookup_error, declared_in[{path,constraint,kind}], edit_sites and edit_site_count. edit_site_count is the input to the surgical ~1-5 SLOC judgement; the tool states NO verdict. Determinism (UUIDv5 serialNumber, no wall-clock timestamp, sorted rows/keys) so a recurring re-run diffs to nothing. AC-SBOM-22. No part of Slice 33 was built.

Design §7 re-verifies from the tree, at cbb56212, that scripts/sbom-survey/** is outside every existing gate: agent-test.sh registers scripts/tests/*.sh one-by-one (25 run_capped lines, no glob) and runs pytest only on src/python/tests and dev/agent-tools/ledgerwatch; ci.yml invokes named scripts with no pytest glob; ruff -> src/python; pyright -p src/python; check.sh compileall -> src/python; ast_scan.py python root -> src/python; test_smoke_scripts.sh -> scripts/release/smoke. Only markdownlint (**/*.md) and lychee see the new README, and both pass. The claim 'landing RED tests turns no existing gate red' is therefore verified, not assumed.
